The seam weeps through `A_seam_m` from the step it exists (D.2, D.14) until wear-in or a seam PATCH (M7; V11 SEAL_SEAM is the VS-A form) — the weld's own P1 tell. **Structural half, returns, seam read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*: `can_join_static(plan)` is published as a pure query returning the first failing reason of the nine structural reasons in LS-15 order — `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED`, `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `SEAM_LIMIT`, `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY`, `POWER_CYCLE`, `STABILITY` — reading no node `hp`, `state`, `forced_mode` or `served_pm` and computing no `surge[]`; `can_join` adds `PORT_ABSENT` (a node-state read) at its LS-15 position and the `surge[]` read-out. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; `seam_view(seam_id)` → `{state, sub_edges[{kind, id}], leak_bp, opening_ids[], cut_sides[]}` is pure *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54 / ASK G10)*: `cut_sides` is empty unless the seam is `CUT` with boundary RAGGED, and then holds one entry per side, `{section_id, cut_holes[{cid, a_hole}], uncapped_open_ends}`, where `cid` is the compartment carrying that side's A_CUT virtual hole (one per former opening), `a_hole` is the hole's CURRENT D.2 area (24 at `hp` 2500; 0 once a Vertical Slice plate install or repair closes it) and `uncapped_open_ends` is the count of that side's fluid ports still `open_end`. 279	**LS-24 — Invariants, FAULTED tiers, bounded work.** Two tiers, and every invariant in this GDD belongs to one. *Structural (hard):* edge endpoint slot out of range or pointing at a tombstone; array lengths disagree; ids not strictly ascending; `next_id ≤ max id`; CSR inconsistent with edges; a seam sub-edge whose SeamRecord is missing — checked after every topology mutator in debug, in `post_restore` in all builds, every run in debug; a violation is a kernel step-invariant failure → FAULTED (dev halts; release returns to the menu; no autosave). Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)`, which records the code, returns the failure to the kernel and, in debug, also halts; no invariant relies on GDScript `assert`, which is stripped from release builds and cannot be caught *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Numeric (soft):* an amount below 0, a field above its documented max, conservation drift ≠ 0, `ΔT` clamped — in release clamp to range, increment `graph_saturations[field]` and continue; in debug `GraphFault.raise` halts. Every test suite asserts `graph_saturations` is all zeros, so a rounding defect still fails CI without ejecting a player from a 40-minute session. 339	*Scope note.* Every formula below is integer arithmetic over the fields of `graph.state` and the immutable tuning table `GraphTuning`; nothing here reads Attention, sanity, rhythm state or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` value (LS-21 — a formula whose inputs include any of those is a Pillar 4 violation, not a tuning choice). **Every numeric default is provisional until spikes S0–S3 and the MVP playtest** (Section H); the time-band figures in D.15 are the acceptance targets the defaults were tuned to, not the other way round. Units are the R1 game units: gas in mGU (`GAS_SCALE` 1000 mGU per GU; 1 GU is the amount that gives 0.1 kPa in a 1-tile volume), volume in tiles, pressure derived in dkPa (standard `STD_PRESSURE_DKPA` 1000, standard O2 partial pressure `STD_O2_PP_DKPA` 210), temperature in mC, power in W which is identically dJ per step, energy in dJ, liquids in mL, integrity in basis points 0..10000, fractions in permille, and — on the gas-flow path only — opening area in milli flow units (`A_m` = 1000 × flow units) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. One step is `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = 6 ticks = 0.1 s at `TICK_RATE` 60; "per step" is the only rate anywhere in this section. Source column vocabulary follows the kernel GDD: `constant` = compiled, changing it is a code change; `data file` = read at boot from `assets/data/life_support_graph.json` into `GraphTuning` (a balance pass edits the file, not the code; a designer-authored float is converted once at boot by `int(round(x × scale))` and never hashed); `calculated` = derived at runtime and never persisted; `state` = a persisted field of `graph.state` (hashed, replicated by summary); `registry` = a locked cross-system fact cited verbatim from `design/registry/entities.yaml`. Three arithmetic rules hold everywhere and are not repeated per formula: (1) **every flux is a non-negative magnitude with an explicit direction**, so integer division is applied only to non-negative operands and truncation is `floor` — written `⌊x⌋`; where a ceiling is wanted it is written `⌈x⌉` and computed as `(num + den − 1) / den` on non-negative operands; the only signed divisions are the two remainder-carrying thermal steps (D.7, D.8), which truncate toward zero and carry the remainder so nothing is lost; (2) **no `sqrt`, `exp`, `pow` or `sin` on the propagation path** — D.15 uses `ln` because it is a design-time estimate evaluated by the test harness, never by the sim; (3) every product the propagation code forms appears in D.13's table with its operand maxima, and the boot assertion there refuses to start a build whose table violates `max_a × max_b < 2^62`.

401	The `atmosphere_derive` formula is defined as:
402	
403	`P = ⌊(n_o2 + n_inert) / (V × GAS_SCALE)⌋` ; `p_o2 = ⌊n_o2 / (V × GAS_SCALE)⌋` ; `o2_pm = ⌊1000 × n_o2 / (n_o2 + n_inert)⌋` (0 when the room is empty)
404	
405	Derived: `band = lookup(value, table LS-7)` with hysteresis — a band is left the step its boundary is crossed in the worsening direction and re-entered only once the value is `H` beyond the boundary in the improving direction (`H_P` = 5 dkPa for `P` and `p_o2`, `H_T` = 500 mC for `T`); the band held at the end of the previous run is the hysteresis memory and is persisted (`band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
406	Derived: `pressure_trend = sign(P − P_prev_run)` ∈ {−1, 0, +1}, from the previous run's derived `P` (`p_prev`, persisted — LS-21 — so a restored run reads the same trend as an uninterrupted one) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

413	| P, p_o2 | int | 0–1500 dkPa | calculated | Total and O2 partial pressure |

415	| H_P, H_T | int | 0–20 dkPa (default 5) / 0–2000 mC (default 500) | data file | Hysteresis margins |

418	**Output Range:** all non-negative; `p_o2 ≤ P` always; `P` for a standard room is 1000 and `p_o2` 210. 471	**Output Range:** `out_scr` 0..400 and `inj_o2 + inj_in` 0..600 at defaults; never negative, never more than the pool or the make-up offer holds, never past either setpoint, never more than the ducts carry. A healthy scrubber (400) outruns one crew (300) by 100 mGU/step; a half-degraded one (200) loses to one crew by 100 — the margin is deliberately thin so that scrubber integrity and scrubber power are both felt. With `path_cap` = 0 (closed valve, cut seam, FAILED duct) the vent is silent and the room is on its own air: the valve verb V5 has an immediate, audible consequence. **Recovery from a patched breach** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a room that lost gas is refilled by its vent at 600 mGU/step shared between the species — O2 first, then inert make-up — and the scrubber's make-up is shared in ascending vent id. Fixture BREACH-RECOVERY (D.15): a `V` 20 room with its vent running and one crew breathing, a RUPTURE hole (`A` 7) open for 600 steps and then patched, reads P 664 / p_o2 145 at the patch, is back in NORMAL (P ≥ 705, p_o2 ≥ 185) after 2,712 steps (4.5 min, by O2 alone) and at both setpoints after about 22,000 steps (37 min); patched after 900 steps (P 542) it takes 18 min to NORMAL and 50 min to the setpoints — slow because one vent and one scrubber carry the whole refill, which is the cost of the breach and not a permanent state. A room with no live vent path keeps the pressure it has. With the scrubber FAILED or unpowered the pool's O2 still reaches the vent (tank stock, until it empties), so `p_o2` returns to its setpoint, but `mk_offer` is 0 and the inert deficit is never filled: total pressure tops out at the O2 setpoint plus the inert partial pressure the room still holds — NORMAL (P ≥ 705) is reachable only if the room kept about 63 % or more of its inert gas (the 600-step BREACH-RECOVERY room does and tops out near 729), otherwise the LOW or DECOMP band persists until the scrubber runs (C2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G4)*. The loss is real and recoverable (P5). Respiration is `R_BREATH × N_crew`, so with two crew the 600 mGU budget leaves 0 net O2 and with four the room falls even with the vent at full tilt (D.15 O2-ROOM-N4).
472	**Example:** scrubber `hp` 5000 (`eff` = 500), `sat` = 1000 → `out_scr` = `⌊400 × 500 × 1000 / 10^6⌋` = 200. Vent: `R_VENT` = 600, `eff_v` = 1000, `pool` = 1,500,000, `SP` = 210, `V` = 20, `n_o2` = 2,900,000, `n_inert` = 15,800,000 (the D.3 room: p_o2 145, inert partial 790), `path_cap` = 800 → `def_o2` = 4,200,000 − 2,900,000 = 1,300,000, `def_in` = 0 → `inj_o2` = `min(600, 1,500,000, 800, 1,300,000)` = 600, `inj_in` = 0. One crew in that room draws 300; net +300 mGU/step, so the room climbs toward 210 at 0.015 dkPa/step — about 7 min from THIN back to NORMAL on one vent. The same vent after a patched breach (`n_inert` = 10,380,000, P 664): `def_in` = 5,420,000 but `inj_in` = `min(600 − 600, …)` = 0 until the O2 deficit closes (step 4,333); the inert make-up then fills the rest at 600 mGU/step.

474	**D.6 Power allocation by tier — island balance and brownout**
475	
476	The `power_allocation` formula is defined as:
477	
478	`avail = S + D` ; `served_k = min( R_k , avail − Σ_{j<k} served_j )` for `k` = 0..4 in order ; `sat_k = ⌊1000 × served_k / R_k⌋` (`R_k` = 0 → 1000)
479	
480	Derived *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `batt_used = max(0, Σ served − S)` drawn from BATTERY stocks in ascending node id, each cell limited to `min(BATT_DIS_CAP, stock_b)`; `charge = min(S − Σ served, CH_CAP, Σ_b (BATT_CELL − stock_b))` when there is surplus (`S > Σ served`), allocated across the batteries in ascending node id with each cell taking at most `BATT_CELL − stock_b`; the surplus that does not fit is not delivered anywhere (power has no inventory, and the reactor burns and heats by `out_w`, not by load), so a full cell stays at `BATT_CELL`, no energy is created and LS-24 never has an overfill to clamp (`graph_saturations` stays 0)
481	Derived: reactor output `S_reactor' = clamp(target, S_reactor − RAMP, S_reactor + RAMP)` where `target = out_w_rated × eff` (0 under SCRAM or fuel starve) — the ramp is why `out_w` is persisted
482	Derived: inrush — a LOAD re-energised within the last `INRUSH_STEPS` requests `⌊req_w × INRUSH_PM / 1000⌋` instead of `req_w`
483	Derived: every consumer in tier `k` receives `⌊req × sat_k / 1000⌋` and publishes it as `served_pm = sat_k`; edge load for D.9 is the **net flow** through the edge: `load_e = abs(Σ over nodes v below the edge of (served_v + charge_v − gen_v))` on the island's tree (rooted at the lowest node id, islands are trees by R12), where `gen_v` is the power a source node delivers, dispatched in **merit order** — reactors first, batteries only for what the reactors cannot cover: with `used = Σ served + charge`, `batt_used = max(0, Σ served − S)` and `R_out = used − batt_used = min(S, Σ served) + charge` (the reactors' total delivery), each reactor `i` delivers `⌊S_i × R_out / S⌋` and the integer remainder goes to the lowest reactor id, and each battery delivers its share of `batt_used` in ascending node id (at most `min(BATT_DIS_CAP, stock_b)`); a charging battery is a consumer carrying `charge_b` and is never a source in the same step — a deterministic dispatch, no iteration. The first draft's proportional share `⌊(S_i + D_i) × used / avail⌋` treated a charging battery as a source, so reactor-side cable loads read about 45 % under their true value (hiding real overloads) and the battery's own cable showed a false outflow *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Guard** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G5)*: `S` = 0 gives every reactor `gen` 0, `used` = 0 gives every `gen` 0, and when `avail` = `S + D` = 0 (the reactor SCRAMmed or failed and every cell flat) `gen_i` = 0 for all sources with no division attempted — nothing is served, `sat_k` = 0 for every tier with `R_k` > 0 and every consumer reads `served_pm` 0 (the dark ship of C2 is a defined state, not a 0/0 fault). One source at the root reduces to "the served power below the edge"; two reactors on a welded island share the load in proportion to what they can give, and the seam cable carries only the difference between its side's demand and its side's delivery *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
484	
485	**Variables:**
486	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
487	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
488	| S | int | 0–10000 W | calculated | Sum of source outputs × eff in the island (reactor ramp-limited) |
489	| D | int | 0–Σ over batteries of min(`BATT_DIS_CAP`, stock_b) | calculated | Battery discharge available this step *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
490	| BATT_DIS_CAP | int | 1000–5000 W (default **1000**) | data file (a module-def field once the Item DB carries one) | Discharge limit of one BATTERY node — 1000 W is exactly the tier-0+1 emergency load (scrubber 600 + pump 400), so one cell serves life support and nothing else and a SCRAM sheds lamps, doors and heater at once: the dark, then fog, then frost sequence of LS-7 and C2. At 2000 W one cell carried the whole home-ship demand (about 1,860 W) for about 3 min with no shedding, which deleted that sequence; the first draft named `batt_dis_cap` without defining it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; default changed 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2: the creative-director's lean is tiered shedding)* |
491	| R_k | int | 0–5000 W | calculated | Total requested in tier `k` (0 life-critical: scrubber; 1 pumps; 2 doors; 3 lights and the HEATER — light and heat go first, air and coolant last, so a SCRAM is felt as dark, then fog, then frost; 4 other) |
492	| served_k | int | 0–R_k | calculated | Allocated to tier `k` |
493	| sat_k | int | 0–1000 ‰ | calculated | Satisfaction of tier `k` |
494	| CH_CAP | int | 0–500 W (default 300) | data file | Battery charge rate cap |
495	| RAMP | int | 10–1000 W/step (default 100) | data file | Reactor output change per step |
496	| BATT_CELL | int | 10^6–10^7 dJ (default 3,600,000) | data file (module def) | One battery's full stock = 360 kJ |
497	| INRUSH_PM, INRUSH_STEPS | int | 1000–3000 (default 1500) / 0–20 (default 5) | data file | Re-energise surge magnitude and duration (V3's Attention spike and overload risk) |
498	
499	**Output Range:** tiers are served fully in order; `Σ served ≤ S + D`; no value is negative. The lowest tiers go dark first, and dim in proportion (`sat_3` drives lamp brightness through `served_pm`, P1). A full cell at the tier-0+1 load of the MVP home-ship (1000 W) lasts `3,600,000 / 1000` = 3600 steps = 6 min — the emergency-power clock after a SCRAM; because `BATT_DIS_CAP` equals that load the cell never serves tiers 2–4, so every SCRAM sheds light, doors and heat on the first run *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*.
500	**Example A:** `S` = 2500, `D` = 1000, `R` = [600, 400, 200, 1500, 300] → all 3000 served, `batt_used` = 500. **Example B (SCRAM):** `S` = 0, `D` = 1000 → `served` = [600, 400, 0, 0, 0], `sat` = [1000, 1000, 0, 0, 0]: lamps out, scrubber and pump running on the battery for 6 min. **Example C (inrush):** breaker closed on a branch carrying a 600 W scrubber and 200 W of lamps at `INRUSH_PM` 1500: for 5 steps the branch requests 900 + 300 = 1200 W; on a 1000 W cable that is `ρ` = 1200 → D.9 takes 16 bp/step for half a second — a scorch tick at the box, and a 1200 W spike in `power_use.delta_w_last5` for Attention. **Example D (two sources, the welded island, fixture F-TWO-SRC)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: home reactor `S_a` 2500 W, derelict reactor `S_b` 1500 W, 1800 W of loads (tiers 0–2) on the home side and 1200 W (tier 3) on the derelict side, the seam breaker closed on a seam cable of `cap` 2775: `avail` 4000, `used` 3000; `gen_a` = ⌊2500 × 3000 / 4000⌋ = 1875, `gen_b` = ⌊1500 × 3000 / 4000⌋ = 1125; the derelict-side subtree has served 1200 and gen 1125, so the seam cable carries 75 W (`ρ` 27). With the derelict reactor SCRAMmed (`gen_b` 0, `avail` 2500) tiers 0–2 take their 1800 W and tier 3 gets 700 W: the seam cable carries 700 W (`ρ` 252) — no overload. Derelict Authoring recomputes its own seam-breaker figure (Open Question 24) under this rule. **Example E (one reactor plus a battery, merit order; `S` 2500, one cell)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `Σ served` 2200 with the cell at 1,000,000 dJ: surplus 300, `charge` = `min(300, CH_CAP 300, 3,600,000 − 1,000,000)` = 300, `R_out` = 2500, the reactor delivers 2500 and the cell's cable carries 300 inward; the same island with a full cell: `charge` = `min(300, 300, 0)` = 0, the cell's cable carries 0 and nothing overfills; the reactor derated to `S` 1500 with `Σ served` 1800: `batt_used` 300, `R_out` 1500, the cell delivers 300 (its cable carries 300 outward) and the reactor-side cables carry 1500, their true load. **Example F (`avail` = 0)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G5)*: reactor SCRAMmed (`S` 0), every cell flat (`D` 0), `R` = [600, 400, 200, 1500, 300]: `avail` 0, `served_k` = 0 for all five tiers, `sat_k` = 0, `gen_i` = 0 for every source, `used` 0 — no division, every load reads `served_pm` 0.
501	
502	**D.7 Compartment thermal step — conduction through hull and openings, remainder-carried**
503	
504	The `thermal_step` formula is defined as:
505	
506	`Q_net = Q_src_room + Σ Q_in − Σ Q_out − Q_hull` ; `E = t_rem + 1000 × Q_net` ; `ΔT = clamp( trunc(E / C) , −MAX_DT , +MAX_DT )` ; `t_rem' = E − ΔT × C` ; `T' = T + ΔT` with `C = V × C_TILE`
507	
508	Derived: hull loss `Q_hull = ⌊K_HULL × S_ext × |T − T_amb| / 100000⌋ + ⌊K_HOLE × Σ A_hole × |T − T_amb| / 1000⌋` — an insulated-plate term and a breach-hole term — from the warmer side to the colder; outward loss is added to the section's `radiated_dj`, inward gain subtracted (a signed net counter)
509	Derived: opening conduction `Q_open = ⌊K_OPEN × A_o × |T_i − T_j| / 4000⌋` per OPENING edge (stored or virtual), moved from the warmer compartment to the colder, computed from the start-of-phase snapshot for every edge before any is applied (Jacobi)
510	Derived: the pair `(T, t_rem)` is the conserved quantity `U = T × C + t_rem` in milli-dJ; `T` is its intensive projection — this is how "store extensive, derive intensive" (R1) holds for heat while the readable field stays in mC
511	Derived *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: HEATER thermostat — a HEATER's effective request is `req_eff = ⌊req_w × duty_t / 1000⌋` with `duty_t = clamp( ⌊1000 × (T_SET_MC − T) / T_PROP_MC⌋ , 0 , 1000 )` from its compartment's start-of-phase `T`: the full request at or below `T_SET_MC − T_PROP_MC`, none at or above `T_SET_MC`, linear between; stateless (nothing to persist), applied in phase 2 before the tiers are solved. A closed door has `A_o` = 0 and conducts nothing
512	
513	**Variables:**
514	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
515	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
516	| Q_src_room | int | 0–4000 dJ/step | calculated (D.8: machine waste heat after coolant capture, plus HEATER output, plus footprint CHILL/BURN impulses) | Heat entering the room this step |
517	| K_HULL | int | 10–100 (default **25**) centi-dJ/step/°C per tile (0.25 dJ at default) | data file | Insulated hull conductance — a ship that stays warm on ~1 kW of waste heat needs this below 1 dJ |
518	| K_HOLE | int | 1–10 (default **2**) dJ/step/°C per area unit | data file | Conductance of a breach hole — uninsulated, and the proxy for heat leaving with the gas (R14 forbids advection) |
519	| S_ext | int | 0–80 tiles | state (`exposed_tiles`, cached from Layout) | Exterior-facing hull tiles |
520	| A_hole | int | 0–64 each | calculated (D.2) | Breach hole area |
521	| T, T_o | int | −200000..+150000 mC | state | Room and neighbour temperatures |
522	| T_amb | int | −200000..+150000 (default **−30000**) | data file (`T_AMB_MC`, per world region; one value in MVP) | The exterior's effective radiative sink |
523	| K_OPEN | int | 1–8 (default **4**) | data file | Opening conduction per area unit — 640 dJ/step per 10 °C across an open door, which is what lets one heater warm five rooms |
524	| A_o | int | 0–512 | state / calculated | Opening area |
525	| C_TILE | int | 1000–6000 (default 3000) dJ/°C per tile | data file | Thermal mass per tile |
526	| C | int | 12,000–1,200,000 dJ/°C | calculated | Room thermal mass |
527	| t_rem | int | −C..+C (exclusive) | state | Carried milli-dJ remainder |
528	| MAX_DT | int | 500–5000 (default 2000) mC/step | data file | Per-step clamp; a hit increments `graph_saturations[DT_CLAMP]` — a content bug, not a mechanic |
529	| T_SET_MC | int | 18000–30000 mC (default **22000**) | data file; ★ registry candidate | HEATER thermostat setpoint: above it the heater requests nothing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
530	| T_PROP_MC | int | 500–5000 mC (default **2000**) | data file | Width of the thermostat's proportional band below `T_SET_MC` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
531	| ΔT | int | ±MAX_DT | calculated | Temperature change this step |
532	
533	**Output Range:** `T` is bounded below by `T_amb` (the plate term stops within `⌈100000 / (K_HULL × S_ext)⌉` mC of it — 182 mC for the example room: the thermal truncation stall, expected) and above by the balance between `Q_src_room` and the loss terms, `ΔT_eq = Q_src_room / (K_HULL × S_ext / 100 + K_HOLE × Σ A_hole)` °C above ambient. The plate time constant `τ = 100 × C / (K_HULL × S_ext)` is 16,364 steps = 27 min for the example room on its own — a sealed, unheated room is a slow cold — but a hole of area `A` adds `K_HOLE × A` dJ/°C to a plate conductance of only 5.5, so a RUPTURE hole (`A` 7) cuts `τ` to 4,615 steps and a breached room reaches FROST in 3.9 min and freezes its pipes in 12 min (D.15), which is the cold the player meets. **The healthy baseline is the constraint these defaults were set to:** the MVP home-ship (Σ `S_ext` 80 → 20 dJ/°C of plate loss) keeps every compartment in COMFORT on one 500 W heater plus lamp, scrubber and pump waste (≈ 1,020 dJ/step → about 21 °C uniform against a −30 °C sink, with `K_OPEN` 4 moving 640 dJ/step per 10 °C across each open door); an earlier draft at `K_HULL` ≡ 1 dJ and `T_amb` −40000 lost 1,320 dJ/step per outer room and would have held a *healthy* engine room in FREEZING with its pipes' pre-stage permanently lit — a constantly warning healthy ship, which P1 and P2 forbid. With the heater off (power loss) the whole ship cools with `τ_ship` ≈ 15,000 steps: breath fog at 6 min, frost at 13 min, and — with no hole at all — its liquid pipes show the FREEZE pre-stage at 23 min and freeze solid at 41 min (D.15 SHIP-COLD, the intentional dark-ship clock): the dark is cold and, given time, freezing, and a breach or a derelict brings it forward to 12 min, which is why `T_amb` is −30000 (a sink only 10 °C below `FREEZE_ON_MC`, the Section G build assertion) and not deeper *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Energy is conserved exactly: `Σ U + radiated_dj × 1000` over a section is constant when no machine runs, because every `Q_open` is subtracted once and added once and every `Q_hull` is counted into `radiated_dj`. The remainder is carried, never dropped, so a room 0.5 °C from equilibrium still moves (the stall above is from the hull term's own floor, not from the step). **Thermostat** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the first draft's heater was a fixed 500 W with no thermostat, so closing doors — the main decompression response — left the heater room with nowhere to put its heat and it reached HOT in about 8 min, a healthy ship starting to warn because the player did the right thing (P1, P2). With the thermostat the heater room settles where `500 × duty_t` equals its loss, just under `T_SET_MC` (a sealed 42-tile cryo bay about 21.3 °C), and the HEALTHY uniform equilibrium of the open ship moves from 21 °C to about 20 °C (heater duty ≈ 0.96). The `MAX_DT` saturation of a heater in a 4-tile closet (41 mC per step at full request) is still a content bug, but the room can no longer be driven past `T_SET_MC` by the heater.

534	**Example:** `V` = 30 → `C` = 90,000; `S_ext` = 22; `T` = 40,000; `T_amb` = −30,000; `Q_src_room` = 516 (D.8 example); `t_rem` = 12,500; no openings or holes. `Q_hull` = `⌊25 × 22 × 70,000 / 100,000⌋` = 385 outward; `Q_net` = 516 − 385 = 131; `E` = 12,500 + 131,000 = 143,500; `ΔT` = `trunc(143,500 / 90,000)` = 1; `t_rem'` = 143,500 − 90,000 = 53,500; `T'` = 40,001; `radiated_dj` += 385. Check: `U` before = 40,000 × 90,000 + 12,500 = 3,600,012,500; after = 40,001 × 90,000 + 53,500 = 3,600,143,500; difference 131,000 = 1000 × (516 − 385) exactly. With a RUPTURE hole (`A` 7) in the same room the hole term adds `⌊2 × 7 × 70,000 / 1000⌋` = 980, `Q_net` = −849, and the room cools 9 mC per step.
535	
536	**D.8 Coolant circulation, heat capture, radiator and the machine temperature proxy**
537	
538	The `coolant_loop` formula is defined as:
539	
540	`lvl_f = clamp( (level_pm − L_CAV_LO) × 1000 / (L_CAV_HI − L_CAV_LO) , 0 , 1000 )` ; `circ = ⌊pump_eff × sat × lvl_f / 10^6⌋` ; `Q_cap = min( Q_src , ⌊K_CAP × circ × max(0, T_room − t_cool) / 10^6⌋ )`
541	
542	Derived: radiator `Q_rad = ⌊K_RAD × eff_r × circ × max(0, t_cool − T_amb_r) / 10^9⌋`, added to the section's `radiated_dj`
543	Derived: coolant temperature `E_c = tc_rem + 1000 × (Σ Q_cap − Σ Q_rad)`; `Δt_cool = trunc(E_c / (C_COOL × level_ml))`; `tc_rem' = E_c − Δt_cool × C_COOL × level_ml` (with `level_ml` ≥ 1; at 0 the reservoir carries no heat and `Q_cap` is already 0)
544	Derived: uncaptured heat `Q_src_room = Q_src − Q_cap` enters the machine's compartment (D.7)
545	Derived: machine temperature proxy `T_mach = T_room + ⌊Q_src_room × K_MACH⌋` — the OVERHEAT trigger (LS-11) and the HOT/shimmer pre-stage that opens the fairness window before a SCRAM
546	Derived: `circ` through a path is 0 when any PIPE on it is FAILED (cap 0), any VALVE closed, or the PUMP's node is not OK/DEGRADED; `level_pm = ⌊1000 × level_ml / cap_ml⌋`
547	Derived (guards) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a RESERVOIR with `cap_ml` 0 reads `level_pm` 0 (`circ` 0, no division); `L_CAV_LO ≥ L_CAV_HI` refuses to boot; a PIPE leak debits the reservoir in the same phase 5 before `level_pm` is read, in ascending reservoir id
548	
549	**Variables:**
550	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
551	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
552	| level_ml, cap_ml | int | 0–cap_ml / 5,000–100,000 (default 20,000) | state / data file (module def) | Reservoir fill and rated capacity |
553	| L_CAV_LO, L_CAV_HI | int | 0–399 / 401–1000, LO < HI asserted at boot (defaults 200 / 600) | data file | Below LO the pump cavitates (circ 0); above HI full circulation; the `lvl_f` denominator is `max(1, L_CAV_HI − L_CAV_LO)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
554	| pump_eff, sat | int | 0–1000 | calculated (D.4, D.6 tier 1) | Pump integrity and power |
555	| circ | int | 0–1000 ‰ | calculated | Circulation fraction |
556	| Q_src | int | 0–4000 dJ/step | calculated | Waste heat the jacketed machine produces: `⌊out_w × waste_permille / 1000⌋` |
557	| K_CAP | int | 20–150 (default 75) dJ/step/°C | data file | Jacket coupling |
558	| K_RAD | int | 20–150 (default 60) | data file | Radiator coupling |
559	| eff_r | int | 0–1000 | calculated (D.4) | Radiator integrity |
560	| T_room, t_cool, T_amb_r | int | mC | state / state / data file (`T_AMB_MC`) | Machine room, coolant and radiator-face temperatures |
561	| C_COOL | int | 2–8 (default 4) dJ/°C per mL | data file | Coolant thermal mass per mL |
562	| tc_rem | int | ±(C_COOL × level_ml) | state | Carried remainder |
563	| K_MACH | int | 10–100 (default 40) mC per dJ/step | data file | How far a machine's casing runs above its room per unit of uncaptured heat |
564	| T_mach | int | mC | calculated | Machine proxy temperature |
565	
566	**Output Range:** `circ` 0..1000; `Q_cap ≤ Q_src`; heat not captured stays in the room and in the machine's casing, so losing coolant makes the engine room climb through HOT (1,500 dJ/step against 5.5 dJ/°C of plate loss would head for SCORCH, but door conduction at `K_OPEN` 4 spreads it and the SCRAM below cuts it within 35 s) and the reactor casing hot: at `circ` = 0 with `Q_src` = 1500 and `K_MACH` = 40, `T_mach` = `T_room + 60,000` = 80 °C from a 20 °C room — above `OVERHEAT_ON_MC` 70000, so a stalled pump or a cut coolant line leads to OVERHEAT (sev 3, scorch and shimmer at the casing) and after `OVERHEAT_SCRAM_STEPS` to SCRAM. Every `graph_*` counter named in this section is a **diagnostic: never persisted, never in `canonical_bytes()`, never hashed, never read by sim code**; it is reset at BOOTING and at restore (a restore does not restore it), and the Debug Overlay reads it through the diagnostics channel. 838	- **If two compartments are joined by an opening and the pressure gradient falls below `1 / (G_OPEN × A)` dkPa**: `Δn` floors to 0 and the rooms stop exchanging gas — **equalisation stalls within `⌈1/k⌉` mGU** of exact balance (10,000 mGU = 0.5 dkPa for a pinhole in a 20-tile room; 156 mGU for a door). This is expected behaviour, stated so QA does not file it: the residual is below the 10 dkPa key quantum and below any band boundary's hysteresis, and TD's truncation discipline (floor on non-negative magnitudes) buys exact conservation in exchange for it. Diagnostics: `graph_stall_edges` (count of open edges with `g ≠ 0` and `Δn` = 0 this run; informational; floors apply once, on the final division of D.1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*).

This is the MVP rule (`T_mach` has no inertia of its own; the machine's casing is a proxy, not a store); VS-A may add a persisted machine heat store if playtest wants a SCRAM to cost minutes. Rationale: a one-mGU rounding defect must not eject a player from a 40-minute session, and CI still fails because every suite asserts the counter array is all zeros.
846	- **If `step_no` approaches 2^43** (the RNG key's step field): it cannot — 2^43 steps is 27,000 years at 10 Hz. The assertion `subject_id < 2^20` is the live one; `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192 keeps ids below 2^14 and a build assertion in Section G keeps the cap below 2^20.

1089	## Visual/Audio Requirements
1090	
1091	The Graph draws nothing and plays nothing. It owns the **semantics** that Failure & Trail, In-World Instruments and Adaptive Audio render, and it constrains them:
1092	
1093	- **Descriptors, not visuals.** Every presentation of a failure is derived from a `FailureDescriptor` (mode, medium, severity 0–4, intensity ‰, anchor ids, acoustic class, `alarm_eligible`). Medium selects the art bible's trail word — O₂ → mist, coolant → frost, power → scorch, fuel → drip, integrity → hairline/buckling — and severity selects the band; the Graph never names a colour, a sprite or a sound.
1094	- **One trail per source, continuous along its edge** (art bible rule). A descriptor carries the source anchor and the edge it travels, so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. Trails are on the consequence channel: the Perception Filter can neither remove nor add one, so an orphan trail cannot occur.
1095	- **Spatial gradients are presentation.** Atmosphere is per compartment; frost creeping from a leak point is Failure & Trail's interpolation of the true compartment value plus the leak anchor and its age — honest to the Graph, never a per-tile simulation.
1096	- **Lamps dim honestly.** `served_pm` drives lamp brightness under brownout; a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (P1).
1097	- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum and ticking are read from true values and belong to the consequence channel: a hallucination may neither remove a real hiss nor add a sound in a witness acoustic class (the eight LS-14 ids; WIND is the whistle; there is no loop-whisper class) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from adaptive-audio-and-tells)* (phantom-entity audio is the Filter's own, in its own classes); `alarm_eligible` (severity ≥ 3) is the only state in which an alarm-class sound or the Alarm Red sweep may play — never as the first warning.
1098	- **The first fault the player ever sees** is the seeded coolant frost trail running from the cryo bay leak to the far wall (art bible carried element).
1099	
1100	> 📌 **Asset Spec** — no sprites are owned here; the descriptor→trail mapping table is the input to `/asset-spec system:failure-and-trail-system` once that GDD exists.
1101	
1102	## Game Feel
1103	
1104	The Graph's feel is **slow burn, then cascade, then silence** — and the player should be able to say afterwards exactly why.
1105	
1106	- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship wears: its authored faults run on minute-scale clocks (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue), and the machines that keep it alive wear a little every hour they run (`W_DUTY`), so a fully repaired ship is quiet, never safe. Nothing resolves itself.
1107	- **Long tell, short collapse.** A long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence. The real tells run in minutes (D.15); the sim's own floor beneath them is `W_MIN_WARNING_S` = 10 s of two-channel physical warning before any loss the ship causes by itself, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary. Horrors and the web have their own tells (Attention, Horror Entities) that must precede anything they do to the ship.
1108	- **Every fix moves a cost.** Power for air (the scrubber draws, the web watches); air for heat; a sealed door for a stranded room; a weld for a leaky seam; a salvaged battery for a dark ship. Triage of five coupled loops, not a repair list.
1109	- **Derelicts are already dead.** They don't tick until the player brings power; then faults that wake wear twice as fast (the wear clock, not the leaks and not the drains) — but still warn first *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a breach is already past its tell by the time the hull gives.
1110	- **Rooms never quite settle.** A faint draught at a nearly-shut hatch is real and stays; two rooms do not balance to the last breath. Expected, not a bug.
1111	- **Silence is a tell, and there are two silences** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A leak that has stopped hissing has either nothing left to leak (its descriptor is gone) or a closed valve upstream (the mode stays, `intensity_pm` is 0 and `isolated_at_step` is set). The sound cannot tell them apart; the valve lever can — its position is a TRUTH world-state witness (LS-14) — and so does the trail, which stops growing but stays. Silence alone never means "fixed".
1112	- **The dark has a clock** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A ship left without power does not only go quiet: it goes cold, and with no hole in it at all its coolant and fuel lines freeze solid in about 41 minutes (frost on the lagging first, at 23). Hiding in the dark is a choice with a deadline, and what freezes bursts when it thaws.
1113	
1114	*Anti-targets*: self-healing faults, a rate dial that speeds everything, scripted "if A then B" cascades, dice-roll deaths, a status screen.
1115	
1116	## UI Requirements
1117	
1118	The Graph has no screens. It defines what three diegetic surfaces must be able to show, and forbids a fourth:
1119	
1120	1. **In-World Instruments & Inspect View** — Instruments read values only through `perceived`; the honest needle moves on LS-20 quantum crossings as a one-step ramp (In-World Instruments IW-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)*; a lit inspect card shows one instrument's precise reading and nothing else; gauges are per node, so two instruments on different nodes are the player's "second opinion".
1121	2. **Failure & Trail** — trail spawn/despawn and band changes from `F/`, `C/`, `B/` keys; `T`/`SEC/` for structural rebuilds.
1122	3. **HUD & Suit Layer** — the suit O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the suit's reading of compartment atmosphere via Suit, not a Graph overlay.
1123	4. **Forbidden** — any schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status or loop-summary screen that shows Graph state at a distance. The Debug Overlay (true values) is a development tool and is never shipped as a player surface.
1124	
1125	> **📌 UX Flag — Life-Support Graph**: instruments, inspect card and trail legibility need `/ux-design` for In-World Instruments before epics; stories should cite `design/ux/instruments.md`.

Since edges can't be salvaged, a DESTROYED cable stays SHORT indefinitely as long as a live source feeds it, and the only remedy is opening the upstream breaker — which the player can do. I'll flag this permanent-alarm behavior as a NICE-to-have clarification rather than a correctness issue, since the design already implies the breaker is the escape valve. **Alarm consequence of dead faults (Graph LS-13 (a), routed 2026-10-28).** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* The Graph's alarm gate is `alarm_eligible = alarm_capable(mode) AND sev >= ALARM_SEV_MIN (3) AND gate_open(subject)`. A WORN descriptor is never `alarm_eligible` (LS-11 mode 10: "never `alarm_eligible`"), and STARVE (mode 6) is routed by the Graph as not alarm-capable (a status, not a state change; `[UNV: Graph, the LS-13 (a) wording of capability for mode 6 is the Graph owner's]`), so an authored dead module that carries no live hazard mode never raises the ship alarm on boarding, however its `fail_since_step` or `warn_since_step` are back-dated (M1 sets `has_warn` for any supplied `warn_since_step`, so the gate is open from run 1). Of the four DA-17 dead faults only `j_a_main` (CABLE_JUNCTION, `hp` 2000, breaker open, no load, so no SHORT; D.4 `sev` 1 + floor((7000 - 2000) / 1500) = 4) is in that class: it carries WORN on a served branch or STARVE on the dead bus, and its `alarm_eligible` is false. The other three carry a live mode 1-9 and so are alarm-capable by the Graph's rule: `pa_frozen` (forced FREEZE, `hp` 2500, `sev` 1 + floor(4500 / 1500) = 4), `pb_leak` (LEAK at `intensity_pm` 0, `hp` 2900, `sev` 1 + floor((7000 - 2900) / 1500) = 1 + 2 = 3) and `seg_b_breach` (BREACH, `hp` 0, `sev` 4 capped); each becomes `alarm_eligible` once its gate is open: at once if the template back-dates `warn_since_step` (DA-17 as authored back-dates `fail_since_step` only, so this GDD leaves the gate to the Graph's own 100-step `W_MIN_STEPS` count), otherwise 100 steps after the section's first run. Figures are at the registry defaults `HP_OK` 7000 and `SEV_STEP` 1500 (G4). This GDD takes no position on that and adds no suppression: it states the Graph's truth, so authors do not assume a dead fault is alarm-silent, and a template that wants a silent dead module authors it with no live hazard mode (AC-DA-159).

=====
- **AC-DA-150 (auto)** `G0_SCRUBBER_INSTALL`: GIVEN `home_ship` alone (S0) with `j_cryo` closed, the beacon off, every lamp on and `scr_a` (`hp` 2000, FAILED) installed into `hp_cargo_scrubber` at step 0, WHEN no one intervenes, THEN `scr_a` requests 600 W from step 0 (the DA-47 decided default), `cab_trunk` carries 2480 W at rho_pm 1147 and 8 bp per step, and is DEGRADED at step 376, FAILED at 875 and DESTROYED at 1,250; WHEN the harness opens `j_cryo` at step 800 THEN the trunk carries 1840 W (rho_pm 851, `dhp_ovl` 0), `hp` is 3,600, it is not FAILED, and one zero-part PATCH restores it to `PATCH_CAP_BP`; WHEN `j_cryo` is opened at step 1,000 THEN `cab_trunk` is FAILED (a home blackout) and repairable by a zero-part PATCH while it is not DESTROYED (how long a FAILED trunk keeps burning in SHORT is the Graph's short-burn rule, OQ-DA-53); WHEN no shed happens before step 1,250 THEN it is DESTROYED and `NOT_REPAIRABLE` and the run records the residual run-ender; with the beacon lit the three steps are 334, 778 and 1,112. findings.section: LS-3 / LS-5 / LS-11 / LS-21 (persisted fields)
findings.finding: New this pass. Two pieces of failure state the rules depend on have no persisted field. (1) LS-11 and D.9 say SHORT is 'persisted as the mode flag' and that phase 8 'reads the mode flag persisted by the previous run's phase 9', but the LS-3 / LS-5 persisted lists and LS-21 name no such field. findings.fix: Either derive SHORT in phase 8 from hp and this run's phase-2 island result (it is a pure function of both) and delete 'persisted', or add an explicit persisted flag. Add a persisted u16 dwell counter per OVERHEAT-capable subject (REACTOR, RESERVOIR, LOAD machine) plus an OVERHEAT latch bit to LS-3 and LS-21, and extend AC L1258's list.

findings.section: LS-17 / M19 / Edge Cases 'section is dormant' / AC L1261
findings.finding: Carried over from the last two reviews, not fixed (this pass touched blockers only). The compartment warn trackers warn_since_o2/p/t (LS-13 (b), absolute step stamps) are not in the M19 advance list (LS-17 L224, M19 row L248, Edge Cases L928, AC L1261). On resume the gate counts dormant time as a warning the player witnessed, so alarm_eligible can fire at once for a thin or empty derelict room. That breaks the principle LS-17 states for nodes.
findings.fix: Add warn_since_o2/p/t, for each set bit of warn_bits, to the M19 resume advance, to LS-17, to Edge Cases L928 and to AC L1261 with a numeric case.

findings.section: LS-13 (a) alarm capability: SEVERED (8) and dead authored hazards
findings.finding: Carried over, still unresolved. Mode 8 SEVERED is alarm-capable, and any forced mode takes sev >= 3 (LS-10, LS-11). So the open_end stubs of an ordinary V8 salvage cut (or the player's own M3 cut) become alarm_eligible 100 steps later. The ship alarm, suit.alarm and the HUD sixth mark then fire for something dead and silent that the player caused on purpose, unless they cap every stub. Derelict Authoring L337 documents that its dead FREEZE / LEAK / BREACH faults also alarm on boarding and 'takes no position'. The creative-director's stated position in the last review was that this breaks the tone. No sibling GDD handles the salvage case (grep of Boarding and Interaction is clean).
findings.fix: Record a decision as a delegated ruling: make 8 SEVERED not alarm-capable. For dead authored faults, either gate alarm_eligible on a live flow (intensity_pm > 0) or on cause = ENDOGENOUS, or accept it explicitly and add the 'cap your stubs' expectation to Boarding. Update the registry alarm_capable expression and the Suit, HUD and Audio rows to match.

findings.section: Edge Cases 'If a weld joins a dead section' (L886) vs D.6 / D.9 / LS-11
findings.finding: Carried over, still unresolved. The text says closing the seam breaker onto a FAILED CABLE_JUNCTION 'energised → SHORT' makes the home-ship's seam cable 'overload per D.9 with its OVERLOAD descriptor from the first step'. No formula draws short current. A FAILED junction has cap 0 and splits the island (D.6, D.9). The new LS-11 SHORT is a mode flag with no load term, so it does not create ρ > 1000 on the neighbouring cable. The promised scorch tell has no mechanism.
findings.fix: Rewrite to what the numbers do: closing the breaker merges the islands; the FAILED junction splits it again; the junction reads SHORT (sizzle, alarm-capable) while a live source is behind it; no overload on the seam cable. Or add an explicit short-current term to D.6 / D.9 and an AC.

findings.section: LS-26 'Waits for VS-A', D.16 Example
findings.finding: Carried over twice, still unresolved. LS-26 (L283) still lists 'the hook stagger' under 'Waits for VS-A', and the D.16 Example (L816) still says 'the stagger would put about 0.3 ms on each of three ticks'. LS-8, D.16 rung 1, the Dependencies row and AC L1155 all make offsets 0/2/4 the MVP baseline. An implementer reading LS-26 could drop the stagger.
findings.fix: Delete 'the hook stagger' from the VS-A list in LS-26 and rewrite the D.16 Example in the indicative ('puts about 0.3 ms on each of three ticks').

findings.section: D.5 Example (L472), D.1 Output Range (L365)
findings.finding: Carried over, two arithmetic slips remain. (1) D.5 says the room climbs 'about 7 min from THIN back to NORMAL'. At +0.015 dkPa/step, 145 to 185 is 2,667 steps = 4.4 min, and 7.2 min is the time to the 210 setpoint. (2) D.1 says a 20-tile room 'empties through an open hatch in about 160 steps = 16 s'. 1/k = 156 steps is the e-folding time, and the D.15 DOOR-BREACH row gives VACUUM at 360 steps.
findings.fix: D.5: 'about 4.4 min back to NORMAL (185 dkPa) and 7.2 min to the 210 setpoint'. D.1: 'falls by 1/e in about 160 steps = 16 s (LOW in 5.6 s, VACUUM in 36 s)'. Grep Suit and Audio for a quoted '7 min'.

findings.section: D.15 HEALTHY 'For alarms' (L780) vs AC L1191
findings.finding: Carried over. The text says that at ATMO_COLD FREEZING 'the annunciator sounds after the 100-step gate'. The t tracker opened at COOL (sev 1) minutes earlier, so the gate is already open by the time FREEZING (sev 3) is reached. The clause is also untested: AC L1191 whitelists ATMO_COLD but never asserts when alarm_eligible turns on.
findings.fix: Reword to 'alarm_eligible is true on the first run the band reaches FREEZING (the t tracker has been open since COOL)'. Add one assertion to AC L1191 for a room that cools through COOL, FROST and FREEZING.

findings.section: D.14 q row (L735) vs Modular Ship Assembly D.1 / registry weld_quality
findings.finding: Carried over: owner conflict. The Graph says 'Assembly clamps once: Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)/10))'. The registry owner (Assembly MSA D.1 L536; entities.yaml L5132-5141) uses ceil(LEAK_HP/10) only, and the registry still carries a note that it declines the Graph's form 'until the owner conforms'. findings.fix: Rewrite the q row to cite Assembly's form and keep the Graph's boot check as a cross-check: 'GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING refuses 10 x Q_MIN < max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)'. findings.finding: Carried over (spike-gated, so only the structure is flagged). D.16's own estimate for the largest single hook is about 0.6 ms, above the 0.5 ms P99 spike share. findings.section: Sibling anchors 'LSG:NNN' (about 1,000 cites in 16 GDDs)
findings.finding: Carried over and worse. Failure & Trail, Adaptive Audio, Attention, Boarding, Derelict Authoring, Item DB and others cite this GDD by line number (for example F&T L524 'LSG:158' and 'LSG:201'; Audio 'LSG:649', 'LSG:752', 'LSG:772', 'LSG:1110'). findings.section: systems-index.md rows vs Dependencies (L969-981)
findings.finding: Carried over. findings.fix: Add 'Life-Support Graph' to the Depends On column of those eight rows. The index is a different file, so send it to that file's writer under G6.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: D1 bot (L1299)
findings.finding: Carried over. Quote: 'by step 18,000 the ship's own clocks have produced a live descriptor of sev >= 3 (the authored faults run 4.5-12 min, D.15), so a bot that hides cannot reach the end of the window'. F-MVP carries the authored faults, so this passes whatever the bot does; it does not test the sealed-room strategy it names.
findings.fix: Rewrite as two assertions. (a) On F-MVP-HEALTHY (no authored faults) the sealed-room bot keeps band_o2 NORMAL for 18,000 steps while the scrubber, reactor and fuel last. (b) With the scrubber unpowered at step 1,200 it reaches band_o2 THIN and a sev >= 3 descriptor by the D.15 O2-ROOM clocks plus 5% (THIN at about step 2,000 after the cut).

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria 'Gaps / untestable as written' (L1310-1312) and review-only ACs (L1273, L1305)
findings.finding: Carried over: items that are not pass/fail. L1310 'the MVP playtest reports that average players die without seeing phase B, THEN the Section G knobs are retuned and the D.15 table regenerated' is a hypothesis and a process step. L1311 'WHEN the kernel's dirty-key parameter type is confirmed, THEN either the int form is adopted or the string family form replaces it' is a decision, not a test. L1312 'each has its own criteria; none is testable at MVP and none is claimed here' is not an AC. L1273 and L1305 are (review) only.
findings.fix: L1310: move to Open Question 12 or rewrite as '(manual) GIVEN >= 3 testers, THEN the logged time from first sev >= 1 descriptor to death has median 4-12 min; outside it the D.15 targets are re-opened'. L1311: '(auto) GIVEN the kernel dirty-key type is int, THEN (KIND << 32) | id round-trips for KIND 1..9, id < 2^20; if String, THEN the string form is used and no other rule changes' (or move to OQ 20-series). L1312: delete. L1305: make it an (auto) registry lint listing the star knobs and their defaults. L1273: (lint) that no mutator parameter type is in the believed-state set.

findings.section: LS-11 SHORT / D.9 short burn: DESTROYED cable
findings.finding: New this pass. The SHORT predicate 'hp <= HP_FAIL while energised' also holds at hp 0. findings.fix: Add one sentence to LS-11 and D.9: 'a DESTROYED cable stays SHORT (and alarm-capable) while a live source is behind it; the only remedy is M9 on the upstream breaker, and there is no replace verb for a DESTROYED edge at MVP'. findings.fix: Add a one-line note in D.9 that shedding load does not end SHORT, and route it to Derelict Authoring: close OQ-DA-53 (a) and change L337 to 'no live source behind it'.

Add a persisted u16 dwell counter per OVERHEAT-capable subject (REACTOR, RESERVOIR, LOAD machine) plus an OVERHEAT latch bit to LS-3 and LS-21, and extend AC L1258's list.

findings.section: LS-17 / M19 / Edge Cases 'section is dormant' / AC L1261
findings.finding: Carried over from the last two reviews, not fixed (this pass touched blockers only). The compartment warn trackers warn_since_o2/p/t (LS-13 (b), absolute step stamps) are not in the M19 advance list (LS-17 L224, M19 row L248, Edge Cases L928, AC L1261). findings.section: LS-13 (a) alarm capability: SEVERED (8) and dead authored hazards
findings.finding: Carried over, still unresolved. Mode 8 SEVERED is alarm-capable, and any forced mode takes sev >= 3 (LS-10, LS-11). So the open_end stubs of an ordinary V8 salvage cut (or the player's own M3 cut) become alarm_eligible 100 steps later. The ship alarm, suit.alarm and the HUD sixth mark then fire for something dead and silent that the player caused on purpose, unless they cap every stub. Derelict Authoring L337 documents that its dead FREEZE / LEAK / BREACH faults also alarm on boarding and 'takes no position'. The creative-director's stated position in the last review was that this breaks the tone. No sibling GDD handles the salvage case (grep of Boarding and Interaction is clean).
findings.fix: Record a decision as a delegated ruling: make 8 SEVERED not alarm-capable. For dead authored faults, either gate alarm_eligible on a live flow (intensity_pm > 0) or on cause = ENDOGENOUS, or accept it explicitly and add the 'cap your stubs' expectation to Boarding. Update the registry alarm_capable expression and the Suit, HUD and Audio rows to match.

findings.section: Edge Cases 'If a weld joins a dead section' (L886) vs D.6 / D.9 / LS-11
findings.finding: Carried over, still unresolved. The text says closing the seam breaker onto a FAILED CABLE_JUNCTION 'energised → SHORT' makes the home-ship's seam cable 'overload per D.9 with its OVERLOAD descriptor from the first step'. No formula draws short current. A FAILED junction has cap 0 and splits the island (D.6, D.9). The new LS-11 SHORT is a mode flag with no load term, so it does not create ρ > 1000 on the neighbouring cable. The promised scorch tell has no mechanism.
findings.fix: Rewrite to what the numbers do: closing the breaker merges the islands; the FAILED junction splits it again; the junction reads SHORT (sizzle, alarm-capable) while a live source is behind it; no overload on the seam cable. Or add an explicit short-current term to D.6 / D.9 and an AC.

findings.section: LS-26 'Waits for VS-A', D.16 Example

findings.section: D.5 Example (L472), D.1 Output Range (L365)
findings.finding: Carried over, two arithmetic slips remain. (1) D.5 says the room climbs 'about 7 min from THIN back to NORMAL'. At +0.015 dkPa/step, 145 to 185 is 2,667 steps = 4.4 min, and 7.2 min is the time to the 210 setpoint. (2) D.1 says a 20-tile room 'empties through an open hatch in about 160 steps = 16 s'. 1/k = 156 steps is the e-folding time, and the D.15 DOOR-BREACH row gives VACUUM at 360 steps.
findings.fix: D.5: 'about 4.4 min back to NORMAL (185 dkPa) and 7.2 min to the 210 setpoint'. D.1: 'falls by 1/e in about 160 steps = 16 s (LOW in 5.6 s, VACUUM in 36 s)'. Grep Suit and Audio for a quoted '7 min'.

findings.section: D.15 HEALTHY 'For alarms' (L780) vs AC L1191
findings.finding: Carried over. The text says that at ATMO_COLD FREEZING 'the annunciator sounds after the 100-step gate'. findings.fix: Reword to 'alarm_eligible is true on the first run the band reaches FREEZING (the t tracker has been open since COOL)'. Add one assertion to AC L1191 for a room that cools through COOL, FROST and FREEZING.

findings.section: Cross-References rationale-tag glossary (L1138); all uses of 'R12'-'R24'

findings.finding: Carried over (spike-gated, so only the structure is flagged). D.16's own estimate for the largest single hook is about 0.6 ms, above the 0.5 ms P99 spike share. findings.finding: Carried over: items that are not pass/fail. findings.section: LS-11 SHORT / D.9 short burn: DESTROYED cable
findings.finding: New this pass. The SHORT predicate 'hp <= HP_FAIL while energised' also holds at hp 0. A DESTROYED cable with a live source behind it therefore keeps a sev-4, alarm-capable SIZZLE descriptor for ever, until the player opens the upstream breaker. A DESTROYED edge also has no replace path (M5 and M6 act on nodes; the Edge Cases 'salvage then install' route does not cover CABLE / PIPE / DUCT edges). Derelict Authoring AC-DA-150 already records this as a 'residual run-ender'. The GDD never states either consequence.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to LS-11 and D.9: 'a DESTROYED cable stays SHORT (and alarm-capable) while a live source is behind it; the only remedy is M9 on the upstream breaker, and there is no replace verb for a DESTROYED edge at MVP'. Add a case to AC L1202 (opening the breaker after DESTROYED clears SHORT).

findings.section: Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-53 (a) and DA L337 vs LS-11 / D.9
findings.finding: New this pass, sibling check. DA still lists as open (OQ-DA-53 (a)) whether shedding the downstream load ends the SHORT on cab_trunk. The Graph's new predicate answers it: the cable stays SHORT while an end island holds a live source, so shedding load does not end it; only the upstream breaker or repair does. DA L337 also gives 'no load, so no SHORT' as the reason a breaker-open junction is quiet, whereas the Graph's reason is 'no live source behind it'. AC-DA-150's figures (8 bp/step: 376 / 875 / 1,250) match the Graph.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note in D.9 that shedding load does not end SHORT, and route it to Derelict Authoring: close OQ-DA-53 (a) and change L337 to 'no live source behind it'.

findings.section: LS-14 AIRFLOW liveness (row 24)
findings.finding: New this pass. AIRFLOW is live while area > 0 and ΔP != 0, with ΔP from the floored display pressures, and it has no hysteresis (SEAL_STRAIN does). With intensity now >= 1 per dkPa, a pair of rooms at the end of their equalisation stall can flip the descriptor on and off between 0 and 1 dkPa as the two floors cross integer boundaries. That makes a one-permille hiss pop.
findings.fix: Keep AIRFLOW live until |ΔP| = 0 on 3 consecutive runs, or take the liveness test from the exact gradient g (nonzero while Δn > 0). Add one AC for the stall tail.

data.summary: Both prior blockers are RESOLVED, and I found no new BLOCKING defect. (1) Blocker 1: SHORT is now `hp <= HP_FAIL` while energised, one predicate shared by the mode and the burn. I recomputed the PWR-OVL timeline (FAILED and SHORT at step 1750, burning steps 1751..2500, DESTROYED at 2500; DERELICT 875 / 1250; breaker opened at 1760 leaves hp 2960). It matches D.9, D.15 and ACs L1202-1203, and Derelict Authoring AC-DA-150's figures agree. (2) Blocker 2: AIRFLOW intensity is `min(1000, |dP|)` in dkPa, never 0 while live, and the old `/ 1000` form is gone from the whole design/ tree; the F&T / Audio silence rules no longer silence the draught. The script checks: the receipt reports CHANGED for the GDD and the registry; the structure check shows all 8 sections PRESENT; only the four undesigned VS systems have no GDD (R9, not blockers). The rest of the GDD is internally consistent at registry defaults: I spot-checked D.1, D.2, D.4, D.5, D.7, D.8, D.9, D.11, D.14 and D.15 numbers and the matching ACs and found no error beyond the two known slips (NICE/REC items above). The 'confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20)' markers and the R12 machines are consistent with project.yaml qa.min_spec, and no 'USER DECISION' or 'pending user confirmation' text remains. Remaining work is 15 RECOMMENDED and 4 NICE items, mostly stale or contradictory wording that earlier fix passes left alone because they only handled blockers. The most important are: persistence of the SHORT flag and the OVERHEAT dwell counters (new this pass), the compartment warn trackers on dormant resume, the alarm capability of SEVERED stubs and dead faults, and the untestable ACs, which I quote with rewrites. Verdict: APPROVED with recommended revisions (no blockers).
